title: U.S. House · Tennessee's 8th District
area: West Tennessee, including parts of Memphis's suburbs, Jackson, and Martin, under the congressional map Tennessee redrew in May 2026.

context.text: Tennessee redrew its congressional district boundaries in May 2026 (mid-decade redistricting). Incumbent Rep. David Kustoff (R) was unopposed in the August 6, 2026 Republican primary. Heidi Kuhn won the Democratic primary with 51.8% of the vote in a four-candidate field. Seven independent candidates are also on the general-election ballot.
Ballotpedia has not published outside race ratings for this district for the 2026 cycle at the time of research; Kustoff has won this seat in five straight elections since 2016.

candidates.name: David Kustoff
candidates.ballotNote: Unopposed in the August 6 Republican primary

summary.text: David Kustoff has represented Tennessee's 8th District since 2017. A Memphis attorney and former U.S. Attorney for the Western District of Tennessee, he serves on the House Ways and Means Committee.

background.text: Born and raised in Shelby County; graduated from the University of Memphis and its Cecil C. Humphreys School of Law in 1992, then opened a Memphis law firm.
Served as Chairman of the Shelby County GOP (1995–1999) and Tennessee chairman of the Bush/Cheney presidential campaigns in 2000 and 2004.

Appointed U.S. Attorney for the Western District of Tennessee by President George W. Bush in 2006; oversaw the Tennessee Waltz public-corruption trials that sent 12 defendants, including a state senator, to federal prison.
Appointed by Gov. Bill Haslam to the Tennessee Higher Education Commission in 2015, overseeing implementation of the Tennessee Promise community-college scholarship program.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2016 and re-elected in 2018, 2020, 2022, and 2024.

positions.summary: States he is committed to protecting Second Amendment rights and opposes gun-control legislation; voted against gun-control bills in Congress.
positions.quote: I believe that our Second Amendment right to keep and bear arms is one of the most important rights granted in the Constitution. As your Congressman, I remain committed to protecting and defending the Second Amendment rights of all law-abiding citizens in West Tennessee.

positions.summary: States he opposes legal abortion and supports policies restricting it.
positions.quote: I believe that life begins at conception and that abortion is wrong. As your Representative, I will continue to back pro-life policies that protect the lives of unborn children and the well-being of their mothers.

record.text: Voted against gun-control legislation in the House, saying the bills "trespass on the Second Amendment" and "place more restrictive burdens on law-abiding gun owners."
Serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means, including its Tax and Health subcommittees.

candidates.name: Heidi Kuhn
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 6 Democratic primary with 51.8% of the vote in a four-candidate field

summary.text: Heidi Kuhn is the Shelby County Criminal Court Clerk and the Democratic nominee for the 8th District. She describes herself as focused on lowering costs and expanding opportunity for West Tennessee families.

background.text: Currently serves as Shelby County Criminal Court Clerk.

priorities.text: Says lowering the cost of living for working families is her top priority, citing groceries, housing, healthcare, and child care costs.
priorities.quote: Lowering the cost of living for working families is my top priority. Families across West Tennessee are working hard but continue to struggle with the rising costs of groceries, housing, healthcare, child care, and other everyday expenses.

priorities.text: Says supporting farmers and strengthening rural communities is a top priority, including protecting family farms and expanding rural infrastructure.
Says protecting workers' rights and supporting organized labor is a key priority.
priorities.quote: Every worker deserves fair wages, safe working conditions, and the freedom to organize and bargain collectively.

positions.summary: Says every worker deserves fair wages and the freedom to organize and bargain collectively, and supports policies protecting the right to organize.
positions.quote: Every worker deserves fair wages, safe working conditions, and the freedom to organize and bargain collectively.

summary.text: Adam Austill is an independent candidate from Covington, Tennessee, a doctoral candidate at the University of Memphis studying American literature who works with children with autism providing ABA therapy.

background.text: Doctoral candidate at the University of Memphis studying American literature; works providing ABA therapy for children with autism.

priorities.text: Proposes public financing of elections, ending congressional stock trading, and twelve-year term limits to limit the influence of money in Congress.
Calls for firm restrictions on artificial intelligence, including on AI-powered surveillance and data-center resource use.

summary.text: Pamela Moses is an independent candidate who describes herself as a musician, human-rights advocate, and voting-rights activist; she says a past conviction bars her from voting even though she can run for office.

background.text: Says she is a human-rights advocate who has challenged voter-disenfranchisement laws affecting people with past convictions.

priorities.text: Campaign focuses on equal justice under the law and voting-rights restoration for people with past convictions.

summary.text: Horace Taylor is an independent candidate who describes himself as independent of party loyalty, saying he would evaluate votes on whether they move things forward for West Tennesseans.
summary.quote: I will not be boxed in by party loyalty. I am "Independent" and independence is your greatest asset in Congress.

priorities.text: Says he would break from straight party-line voting and evaluate each vote on whether it benefits West Tennesseans.
